memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Sarah said, "God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears about this will laugh with me." And she added, "Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age." - Gen 21:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Listen to the wonder in Sarah's voice: "God has brought me laughter." This is no longer the bitter, disbelieving laugh of a worn-out heart. This is pure joy overflowing. And she wants everyone to share in it: "everyone who hears about this will laugh with me." Her joy is so full it cannot be contained; it spills out to include others.

There is something beautiful about the way God's blessings produce shared joy. Sarah's miracle wasn't just for her; it was a gift meant to gladden a whole community. When God does something wonderful in our lives, it becomes a testimony that lifts and encourages others too.

Notice Sarah marvelling at the sheer improbability: "Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children?" She never gets over the wonder of it. She keeps circling back to how impossible it was, how utterly beyond her - because that is exactly what makes it so clearly the work of God.

This is a good posture for us to keep: never getting over the wonder of what God has done. It is easy to grow used to God's blessings and forget the amazement they should stir. But Sarah models a heart that keeps marvelling, keeps rejoicing, keeps giving God the glory. "The Lord has done great things for us, and we are filled with joy" (Ps 126:3). What has God done in your life that you should marvel at afresh today?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you grown used to God's blessings, or do you still marvel at them?
- How can your joy in God's goodness become an encouragement to others?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You for the laughter and joy You bring. Keep me from growing used to Your blessings; help me never get over the wonder of what You have done. Let my joy overflow to encourage others.
Amen.
